title: Geometric Pricing: How Low Dimensionality Helps in Approximability

venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2012-07-24; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: For the stated geometric pricing variants and fixed dimension d, gives O~_d(n^(1-epsilon(d))) with epsilon(d)=1/4^(d-1) as presented in the paper, plus dimension-2 QPTAS results; reports hardness already in small dimensions and APX-hardness by dimension four for variants. The exponent advantage shrinks rapidly with d; model assumes attribute-induced conjunctive screening. Theorem only; no deployment evaluation.

title: Truthful Mechanisms for Matching and Clustering in an Ordinal World

venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2016-10-18; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: Universally truthful ordinal ratios include 1.7638 for weighted perfect matching, 2 for max k-matching and k-sum clustering, and 2 for Max TSP only for metric hidden weights; densest k-subgraph has a 6-approximation with separate bicriteria option. Non-truthful ordinal alternatives improve some ratios (e.g., weighted matching 1.6 and Max TSP 1.88) but drop incentive compatibility. Formal proof results, not measured preference-elicitation outcomes.

venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2021-08-09; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: For undirected graphs with n vertices, m edges and component diameter <=D, proves deterministic O(log D + log log_{m/n} n) rounds with O(n^delta) local space per machine and O(m+n) global space. Conditional Omega(log D) bound relies on the 1-vs-2-cycles conjecture. The algorithm is explicitly not component-stable; theorem concerns MPC asymptotic complexity, not measured cluster wall time.

title: Weighted k-Server Admits an Exponentially Competitive Algorithm
review_status: full-text audit complete; competitive-ratio theorem restricted to weighted uniform metrics, with memory/runtime trade-off left distinct
sections_checked: uniform versus arbitrary metric weighted k-server problem definition

venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2025-10-26; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: Proves exp(O(k^2))-competitive randomized algorithm for weighted k-server on uniform metrics; weight rounding costs at most 2^(k-1) in ratio and a generalized problem receives the same asymptotic guarantee. Does not solve arbitrary metrics; for general k>2 no competitive algorithm is known per the paper. Authors call out computational efficiency and memory-vs-ratio as open; competitive ratio alone is not an implementation-efficiency result.
